methodologyNotes: Specs were read from GSMArena spec pages (primary, machine-readable) and corroborated against official manufacturer pages, manufacturer newsrooms, Wikipedia, and reputable launch coverage (9to5Google, Android Authority, fonearena, Optus device help). Numbers are stored unit-free; units are implied by the spec key (display_in = inches, refresh_hz = hertz, ram_gb/storage_gb = gigabytes, main_camera_mp = megapixels, battery_mah = milliamp-hours, charge_w = watts, weight_g = grams). display_in is the diagonal screen size. refresh_hz is the maximum panel refresh rate (for the Asus Zenfone 12 Ultra this is the 144 Hz gaming ceiling over a 120 Hz everyday LTPO mode). ram_gb and storage_gb are the lowest globally announced base configuration, which may differ from the lowest US-sold config. os is the OPERATING SYSTEM AT LAUNCH, not the current shipping version (GSMArena and Apple now show post-launch updates such as iOS 26 / One UI 8). main_camera_mp is the primary rear sensor only. priceUsd is the US launch MSRP in USD for the base configuration noted in priceNote. GSMArena's on-page price rows are EUR-converted estimates and were NOT used as MSRP; US MSRP came from official manufacturer pages or launch press. Fallback policy: where a phone was never officially sold in the US (Xiaomi 15, Samsung Galaxy A55, Asus Zenfone 12 Ultra), priceUsd is null and the reason is given in priceNote and provenance rather than reporting a grey-market import price. Where an official spec sheet omits a number (e.g. iPhone 60 Hz panels, Apple wired wattage), the well-established hardware figure is used and flagged in provenance. A null is preferred over any guess. accessedAt is 2026-06-15 on every source.

products.name: Apple iPhone 16 Pro
products.provenance: Specs read from the GSMArena spec page and corroborated against Wikipedia. The $999 US MSRP (128GB) came from Wikipedia/launch coverage because Apple's live spec page now redirects to newer-iPhone marketing and exposes no price, and GSMArena only shows a EUR-converted estimate. OS reported as the launch version iOS 18 (Apple's page now lists a later iOS). Nothing was nulled.

products.name: Apple iPhone 16
products.provenance: Specs from GSMArena, corroborated by Apple's official spec page. The 60 Hz refresh (no ProMotion) was explicitly confirmed on Apple's spec page. The $799 US MSRP (128GB) came from launch coverage/Wikipedia since GSMArena shows only a EUR-converted estimate. charge_w 25 per GSMArena; Apple markets a 20W+ adapter. OS is the launch iOS 18. Nothing was nulled.

products.name: Apple iPhone 16e
products.provenance: Specs from GSMArena, price from Apple's official newsroom ('starting at $599 (U.S.)' for 128GB). GSMArena's printed price was a misrendered conversion and was discarded. refresh_hz 60 (no ProMotion) and charge_w 20 are the established hardware figures; Apple's marketing does not print an explicit max wattage. The 16e uses a binned A18. OS is the launch iOS 18. Nothing was nulled.

products.name: Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra
products.provenance: Specs from GSMArena, price verified directly on Samsung's official US buy page ($1,299.99 for the 256GB base, the smallest US config). Launch OS is Android 15 with One UI 7 (GSMArena now lists the One UI 8 update). Chipset is the overclocked 'Snapdragon 8 Elite for Galaxy'. Nothing was nulled.

products.name: Samsung Galaxy S25
products.provenance: Specs from GSMArena, price verified on Samsung's official US store ($799.99 regular for the 128GB base; a $699.99 figure seen elsewhere is a promotional discount, not MSRP). Launch OS is Android 15 with One UI 7. Nothing was nulled.

products.name: Samsung Galaxy A55 5G
products.priceNote: 8GB/128GB base config; not officially sold in the US, so no USD MSRP exists
products.provenance: Specs from GSMArena; base RAM corrected to 8GB per official Samsung listings. priceUsd is null because Samsung publicly confirmed it would not sell the A55 in the US, so there is no US launch MSRP; only imported international units exist. Launch OS is Android 14 (One UI 6.1). Nothing else was nulled.

products.name: Google Pixel 9 Pro
products.provenance: Specs from GSMArena (16GB base RAM, 128GB base storage confirmed). The $999 US MSRP (128GB) came from Google's launch and 9to5Google; GSMArena's price row was an unreliable regional artifact and was rejected. Launch OS is Android 14. Nothing was nulled.

products.name: Google Pixel 9
products.provenance: Specs from GSMArena. The $799 base MSRP (12GB/128GB) came from Google's launch and press coverage since GSMArena did not print it. The standard Pixel 9 uses a non-LTPO OLED (LTPO is Pro-only). Launch OS is Android 14. Nothing was nulled.

products.name: Google Pixel 9a
products.provenance: Specs from the correct GSMArena page (ID 13478; the originally supplied ID resolved to an unrelated phone and was discarded). The $499 US MSRP for the 128GB/8GB base came from Google's March 2025 announcement; GSMArena foregrounds the 256GB config but the official base is 128GB. Main rear sensor is 48MP (lower than the Pixel 9's 50MP). Launch OS is Android 15. Nothing was nulled.

products.name: OnePlus 13
products.provenance: Specs from GSMArena, corroborated by OnePlus's US spec page. The $899 US MSRP is for the 12GB/256GB base US config. charge_w is 80W for the US model (the 100W SUPERVOOC figure on GSMArena is the global/China rating). releaseDate is the Jan 2025 global/US launch (GSMArena's Nov 2024 is the China announcement). ip_rating reported as IP69 (the phone carries IP68 and IP69); OS is OxygenOS 15 over Android 15. Nothing was nulled.

products.name: Xiaomi 15
products.priceNote: Global base 12GB/256GB; Xiaomi does not officially sell its flagship line in the US, so no USD MSRP exists
products.provenance: Specs from GSMArena and fonearena's global-launch writeup (correct GSMArena ID 13472; the originally supplied ID was wrong). Global model has a 5240mAh battery (the China unit is 5400mAh) and weighs 191g. priceUsd is null because the Xiaomi 15 was not officially sold in the US; US listings near $850 are third-party importers, not an MSRP. releaseDate 2025-03 reflects the global launch (China launch was 2024-10). OS is HyperOS 2 over Android 15. Nothing else was nulled.

products.name: Nothing Phone (3)
products.provenance: This is the 2025 flagship Phone (3), distinct from the Phone (3a) line. Specs read via GSMArena spec content and corroborated against Nothing's official product page (camera, RAM/storage, IP68) and launch coverage (9to5Google, Optus). The $799 US MSRP (12GB/256GB) is a genuine US launch price. International battery is 5150mAh. Panel is LTPS AMOLED (not LTPO). Launch OS is Nothing OS over Android 15. Nothing was nulled.

products.name: Nothing Phone (3a)
products.priceNote: US price $379 via Nothing's US Beta/Developer Program; global base 8GB/128GB

products.name: Motorola Edge (2025)
products.provenance: Specs read via GSMArena spec content (correct ID 13907; the originally supplied ID was wrong) and corroborated by Motorola's US support page and carrier listings. The $549.99 US launch price is for the 8GB/256GB config; lower figures seen now (~$472) are post-launch discounts, not MSRP. Chipset is the Dimensity 7400 (marketed 'Ultra'). Released around June 6, 2025. Launch OS is Android 15. Nothing was nulled.
